rows.name: Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skippedFullShellNonnegative
rows.annotation: If the full-shell margin is nonnegative at every real greedy skipped rank from $3$ onward, then $1/2\in\mathcal A$. The argument `hsign` is exactly that universal condition. Its horizon is specified as the skipped rank itself. The theorem needs no sharpening to the earlier precritical horizon for this conclusion, but supplies no proof that its own margin condition holds.

rows.name: Erdos249257.cofinalExactLocalMersenneHalfRows_of_positiveHalfGreedySkips
rows.annotation: Arbitrarily late positive skips of the half-greedy rule yield exact quotient rows at unbounded depths. The only input is `hskips : CofinalPositiveHalfGreedySkips`. A skip at rank $c\ge4$ provides an exact row at depth $2c-2$, so unbounded skipped ranks give unbounded row depths. The theorem proves this implication. It does not establish the required skips. The separate half-membership equivalences explain why the antecedent remains an unresolved existence condition.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_cpgs_equiv
rows.annotation: Arbitrarily late positive greedy skips are equivalent to representation of $1/2$. The declaration also states that every rational half-greedy remainder is positive, so the positivity condition can be removed, and identifies the resulting unbounded skips with an infinite skipped support. Its conclusion is a conjunction of these facts and equivalences. All are unconditional, but none asserts that arbitrarily late skips exist. The final conjunct is the displayed equivalence $\mathrm{CPGS}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{HALF}$.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_cpgs_equiv
rows.annotation: Arbitrarily late positive greedy skips are equivalent to representation of $1/2$. The declaration also states that every rational half-greedy remainder is positive, so the positivity condition can be removed, and identifies the resulting unbounded skips with an infinite skipped support. Its conclusion is a conjunction of these facts and equivalences. All are unconditional, but none asserts that arbitrarily late skips exist. The final conjunct is the displayed equivalence $\mathrm{CPGS}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{HALF}$.

rows.name: Erdos249257.HalfCarryReachability.HalfCarryCofinalTerminalOnlyStrip
rows.annotation: The proposition that every bound $N$ admits a depth $M\ge\max(N,1)$ with a terminal-strip witness. The witness is a finite Boolean word with ranks $0,1$ excluded and its terminal integer carry bounded in absolute value by $2\lfloor\sqrt M\rfloor+4$. Different depths may use incompatible words. The definition asks for unbounded existence and provides no witnesses.

rows.name: Erdos249257.HalfCarryReachability.exists_infinite_support_half_of_cofinalTerminalOnlyStrip
rows.plain: Terminal strips produce an infinite support
rows.annotation: An unbounded supply of terminal-strip witnesses yields an infinite support with value exactly $1/2$. The only premise is `hcofinal : HalfCarryCofinalTerminalOnlyStrip`. The finite words may be mutually incompatible, and compactness extracts a limiting representation. Odd denominator parity then excludes a finite representing support. The declaration does not establish the unbounded supply of finite words.

ties.name: Erdos249257.HalfCarryReachability.greedy_half_infinite_of_cofinalStripReturn
ties.plain: Greedy strip returns yield exact value

rows.name: Erdos249257.HalfCarryReachability.greedy_half_infinite_of_cofinalStripReturn
rows.plain: Greedy strip returns yield exact value
rows.annotation: If the actual half-greedy carry returns below its strip bound at unbounded depths, the greedy support is infinite and its value is $1/2$. The argument `hreturn` is the entire cofinal-return condition. The conjunction in the conclusion contains both infinitude and exact value. The theorem applies to the fixed greedy support, rather than an arbitrary support with a few bounded carries.

rows.name: Erdos249257.HalfCarryReachability.infinite_support_half_of_mobiusCenteredHalfCarry_sqrtBound
rows.annotation: A support omitting $0$ and $1$ has infinite support and value $1/2$ if its centred carry is nonnegative and at most $2\sqrt N+4$ at every depth. The assumptions `hzero`, `hone`, `hnonneg` and `hbound` are all stated. For an arbitrary support the nonnegative lower bound cannot be dropped. Greedy-specific theorems later supply it automatically for the actual half-greedy support.

ties.name: Erdos249257.halfGreedy_precriticalSuffix_lt_iff_futureSkipCoverage
ties.plain: Future skip capacity covers the carry

rows.name: Erdos249257.halfGreedy_precriticalSuffix_lt_iff_futureSkipCoverage
rows.plain: Future skip capacity covers the carry
rows.annotation: At a rational half-greedy skipped rank $c\ge4$, the precritical suffix bound is equivalent to the live carry at $2c-4$ being covered by future-skip capacity from $c$ over $c-3$ steps. The hypotheses are `hc` and `hskip`. The capacity is a weighted sum of future skipped positions. This is an exact reformulation of the precritical test, not an estimate supplying sufficient future skips.

ties.name: Erdos249257.exists_skippedCoreExactRow_of_value_above
ties.plain: An above-half support produces a row

rows.name: Erdos249257.exists_skippedCoreExactRow_of_value_above
rows.plain: An above-half support produces a row
rows.annotation: If a finite support in $[2,n]$ has real value above $1/2$, some crossing rank $4\le c\le n$ produces an exact row at $2c-2$. The assumptions `hE` and `habove` give exactly these bounds and the value inequality. No sharp-capacity hypothesis is required. Since the crossing rank is bounded above rather than below, the new endpoint need not exceed the original endpoint.

rows.name: Erdos249257.exactLocalMersenneHalfRow_double_or_recycle
rows.annotation: An exact row at endpoint $n\ge6$ yields either an exact row at $2n-1$ or one at $2c-2$ for some $4\le c\le n$. These are `hn` and `hrow`. The disjunction provides one next row, and its alternatives need not be exclusive. It gives no lower bound making the recycled endpoint exceed $n$, and no assertion that doubling can be repeated indefinitely.

ties.name: Erdos249257.exists_seeded_bounded_double_or_recycle_model
ties.plain: A seed and dichotomy permit boundedness

rows.name: Erdos249257.exists_seeded_bounded_double_or_recycle_model
rows.plain: A seed and dichotomy permit boundedness
rows.annotation: There exists a predicate with a witness at $6$ and the exact double-or-recycle transition shape, yet with bounded witness depths. The existential predicate is realised by $P(n)\iff n=6$. This proves that the seed and transition shape alone do not imply cofinality. It imposes no assertion on the arithmetic set of actual exact rows, which has additional properties.

rows.name: Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_of_weighted_coeff_certificates
rows.annotation: The support series $X_A(b)$ is irrational if weighted coefficient certificates exist for every positive integer $q$. Lean assumes `hb : 2 ≤ b` and `hcert`, which contains the divisibility block, weighted tail bound, positive later coefficient and final inequality. The indices $N,K,L,C$ may depend on $q$. The theorem works for every support and every such base, but does not produce `hcert` for an arbitrary support. At $b=2$ it gives the paper's implication $\mathrm{Cert}(A)\Rightarrow\mathrm{Irrational}(X_A(2))$.

ties.name: Erdos249257.rat_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_greedySkippedSupport_infinite
ties.plain: Rational targets and infinitely many skips

rows.name: Erdos249257.rat_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_greedySkippedSupport_infinite
rows.plain: Rational targets and infinitely many skips
rows.annotation: For a nonnegative rational target $q$, representation is equivalent to the greedy rule skipping infinitely many positive ranks. The source assumes `q : ℚ` and `hq : 0 ≤ q`. `(q : ℝ)` casts the target into the real achievement set. Rationality is used in the direction from representation to infinitely many skips. This theorem generalises the half-target equivalence, while preserving the nonnegative-target requirement.

rows.name: Erdos249257.mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_greedySkippedSupport_infinite
rows.annotation: A nonnegative target is represented if its greedy rule skips infinitely many positive ranks. The source requires both `hx : 0 ≤ x` and `hskips`. Rationality is unnecessary in this direction, so the result applies to every nonnegative real target. All represented sums are nonnegative. The converse for rational targets is a separate theorem and uses the irrationality of the full reciprocal Mersenne series.

rows.name: Erdos249257.finiteErdosSum_den_odd
rows.annotation: Every finite base-$2$ Mersenne sum over a support omitting $0$ has odd reduced denominator. The hypothesis `h0 : 0 ∉ F` excludes the zero exponent. Individual positive-index denominators are odd, and their least common multiple remains odd. This parity fact excludes finite representations of rationals with even reduced denominator, and passing to an infinite sum requires a separate argument.

ties.name: Erdos249257.dyadic_support_fraction_reciprocalMass_diverges_or_gt_one
ties.plain: A dyadic value needs reciprocal mass

rows.name: Erdos249257.dyadic_support_fraction_reciprocalMass_diverges_or_gt_one
rows.plain: A dyadic value needs reciprocal mass
rows.annotation: If an infinite support has value $p/2^c$, then its reciprocal-index sum diverges or is strictly greater than $1$. The hypotheses `hAinf` and `hvalue` impose infinitude and the dyadic rational value. The numerator `p` is an integer and `c` a natural number. This declaration does not give the same strict conclusion for arbitrary odd factors in the denominator.

rows.name: Erdos249257.supportCoeffZeroWindow_length_le_eps_logb
rows.annotation: If the support contains a positive index and has rational value $p/(2^cv)$ with $v>0$, then each $\varepsilon>0$ admits a constant $B\ge0$ bounding every zero-window length by $\varepsilon\log_2N+B$. The hypotheses `hA`, `hv`, `hvalue` and `hε` are explicit. The constant may depend on the support and parameters. This is an upper bound on window lengths, not existence of long zero windows.

rows.name: Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_pairwise_coprime
rows.annotation: An infinite pairwise-coprime support with summable reciprocals has irrational support series at every integer base $b\ge2$. The hypotheses are `hb`, `hA`, `hpair` and `hsum`. Reciprocal summability is a separate assumption from coprimality. In particular, this declaration cannot be applied to all primes merely because distinct primes are coprime. The reciprocal-sum condition must also hold.

rows.name: Erdos249257.SupportSunflowerDichotomy.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_of_orthogonalPetalBouquet
rows.annotation: At base $2$, an orthogonal-petal bouquet support has irrational value if it also satisfies the forced-slot tail-selection condition. The declaration takes two independent assumptions, `hB` and `hselection`. The structural hypothesis controls cores and coprime petals. The selection hypothesis supplies suitable late tails at every required precision. This theorem does not claim that the bouquet structure by itself proves the tail-selection condition.

rows.name: Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_eventuallyPeriodic
rows.annotation: An infinite support that is periodic above a finite threshold has irrational series at every integer base $b\ge2$. The assumptions `hb`, `hm`, `hper` and `hinf` require the base, positive period, eventual periodicity and infinitude. The equivalence in `hper` must hold for every index above the threshold. The theorem therefore allows finite initial changes but does not cover an arbitrary aperiodic tail.

rows.name: Erdos249257.irrational_of_den_mul_abs_sub_tendsto_zero
rows.annotation: A real number is irrational if rational approximants are eventually unequal to it and their reduced denominators times their absolute errors tend to zero. The assumptions `hne` and `h0` state both requirements. A fixed rational target distinct from an approximant has error at least the reciprocal of the product of their denominators. This domain-neutral theorem needs actual reduced-denominator error control, not a lower bound on denominators.

ties.name: Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSum_of_lcm_gap
ties.plain: A growing LCM gap gives irrationality

rows.name: Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSum_of_lcm_gap
rows.plain: A growing LCM gap gives irrationality
rows.annotation: For a strictly increasing positive exponent sequence, irrationality follows if the next exponent minus the LCM of all preceding exponents tends to infinity. The assumptions `ha`, `ha0` and `hgap` state these conditions, with `hb` fixing $b\ge2$. The difference is a natural-number subtraction. This criterion is sufficient. It does not claim that every irrational support has such large exponent gaps.

ties.name: Erdos249257.erdosSupportSeries_rational_iff_exists_temperedCarry
ties.plain: Rationality is a tempered integer carry

rows.name: Erdos249257.erdosSupportSeries_rational_iff_exists_temperedCarry
rows.plain: Rationality is a tempered integer carry
rows.annotation: For every support $A$, its base-$2$ value is rational exactly when a positive integer multiplier admits a tempered integer carry orbit for the divisor coefficients. The declaration has no support hypotheses. Temperedness includes the affine recurrence and decay after division by $2^N$. The equivalence identifies the arithmetic object to exclude for an irrationality proof. It does not assert that no such orbit exists.

rows.name: Erdos249257.temperedBinaryOrbit_eq_scaledTail
rows.annotation: Every tempered integer orbit for a coefficient sequence bounded by its index equals its multiplier times the exact coefficient tail at each depth. The hypotheses are `hgrowth` and `horbit`. Temperedness removes the exponentially growing homogeneous solution of the recurrence. This identifies any possible integer orbit uniquely, but it does not show whether the resulting real tail values are integers.

rows.name: Erdos249257.one_add_mul_card_le_two_mul_shifted_state
rows.annotation: If a finite support subset divides $L>c$, the shifted recurrence and positive next state give $1+v|F|\le2u(L-c-1)$. The assumptions `hcL`, `hpos`, `hrec`, `hFA` and `hFdvd` specify those inputs. The strict condition $L>c$ ensures the sampled coefficient is genuinely at row $L$. The theorem uses a lower bound at chosen common multiples, not a global upper bound.

rows.name: Erdos249257.shifted_state_unbounded_of_infinite_support
rows.annotation: For an infinite support, any positive natural state sequence satisfying the shifted carry recurrence with multiplier $v>0$ is unbounded. The assumptions `hAinf`, `hv`, `hpos` and `hrec` are explicit. No temperedness or tail identity is required. Unboundedness is compatible with linear growth and with decay after division by $2^n$, so it does not itself contradict a rational-value hypothesis.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR20.paper_general_target_gap
rows.annotation: For every real $x$ between $0$ and the full Mersenne sum, nonmembership is equivalent to lying in an internal gap determined by a finite prefix and a next rank. The declaration also proves both endpoints of every such gap achievable. The convex-hull bounds on $x$ are explicit. This is not restricted to rational targets and does not rely on denominator parity for the endpoints.

ties.name: Erdos249257.irrational_or_bpow_mul_eq_intCast_intWeightedErdosSeries_periodic
ties.plain: Periodic signed values have a dichotomy

rows.name: Erdos249257.irrational_or_bpow_mul_eq_intCast_intWeightedErdosSeries_periodic
rows.plain: Periodic signed values have a dichotomy
rows.annotation: For an integer-valued periodic weight and base $b\ge2$, its series is irrational or becomes an integer after multiplication by a power of $b$. The hypotheses `hb`, `hm` and `hper` require the base, a positive period and periodicity at every index. Signed weights are permitted. The theorem retains periodicity and therefore gives no corresponding dichotomy for an arbitrary aperiodic support.

rows.name: Erdos249257.irrational_intWeightedErdosSeries_periodic_of_coeff_nonneg_of_frequently_ne_zero
rows.annotation: A periodic integer weight has irrational series when its divisor coefficients are nonnegative at positive indices and nonzero arbitrarily far out. Besides `hb`, `hm` and `hper`, the assumptions `hc0` and `hne` supply those sign and nonvanishing conditions. This declaration treats nonnegative coefficients. A claim for the nonpositive case needs the corresponding sign-reversed argument or a separate theorem.

rows.name: Erdos249257.irrational_intWeightedErdosSeries_periodic_of_coeff_nonpos_of_frequently_ne_zero
rows.annotation: For an integer base $b\ge2$ and positive period $m$, a periodic integer weight has irrational series if its divisor-sum coefficients are nonpositive at every positive index and nonzero at arbitrarily large indices. This is the negative-sign companion to the nonnegative theorem. The fixed-sign condition concerns the divisor coefficients, not necessarily the original weights, and periodicity of the weights remains a required hypothesis.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_theoremA_half_membership
rows.annotation: Uniform square-root separation at the specified reset ranks implies that one half belongs to the achievement set. The assumption is `h : PaperResetSqrtEscape`. It covers every eligible reset from row ten onwards. The proof converts the real threshold to the squared bound and feeds the late-step argument. Finite computations at many reset rows do not supply this quantified hypothesis, and the theorem gives no converse from half-membership to the reset estimate.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.resetCrossingBound
rows.annotation: The integer bound is $B(r)=2^{\lfloor(r+4)/2\rfloor}+2r+3$. Natural-number division implements the floor in the exponent. A separate theorem proves $B(r)^2\le2^{r+5}$ for $r\ge10$. The crossing argument bounds an offending deviation by this $B(r)$. This is a ceiling arising from the recurrence, distinct from the strict lower bound that the reset escape hypothesis would supply.

ties.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_theoremA_crossing_bound_square_le
ties.plain: The crossing bound fits the threshold

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_theoremA_crossing_bound_square_le
rows.plain: The crossing bound fits the threshold
rows.annotation: For every $r\ge10$, the explicit bound $B(r)=2^{\lfloor(r+4)/2\rfloor}+2r+3$ satisfies $B(r)^2\le2^{r+5}$. The hypothesis is `hr : 10 ≤ r`. The reset theorem uses this comparison to show that its strict lower bound is incompatible with a crossing estimate of size at most $B(r)$. It is not an estimate for the orbit’s deviation by itself.

ties.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_theoremA_right_branch_forces_small_deviation
ties.plain: A crossing bounds the reset deviation

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_theoremA_right_branch_forces_small_deviation
rows.plain: A crossing bounds the reset deviation
rows.annotation: At a first crossing of the largest omitted rank $d$, a right transition forces $|\Delta_{d+1}|\le B(d)$. The statement requires `hs14`, the largest-rank condition `hd`, lateness `hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d`, the next-step crossing `hcross` and a right branch `hR`. The natural absolute value `natAbs` represents the magnitude of an integer deviation. These hypotheses identify a particular crossing, not every row.

rows.fidelity_note: The cited conjunct excludes every real target $x$ whenever a rank has remainder greater than its full tail; the paper states only $x = 1/2$.
rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_one_sided_finite_decision_boundary
rows.annotation: The cited conjunct excludes every real target $x$ whenever a rank has remainder greater than its full tail. The paper states only $x = 1/2$.

rows.fidelity_note: The last conjunct gives this necessary survival condition for every real x, not just the half target.
rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_one_sided_finite_decision_boundary
rows.annotation: For every real target $x$, membership is equivalent to $x\ge0$ and a remainder no larger than the complete tail at every rank. The last conjunct gives this necessary survival condition for every real $x$, not just the half target.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_centred_completion_of_fixed_precision
rows.annotation: Any finite list of valuations and odd unit residues can be completed to a bounded sequence of successor states. The hypotheses `hu : 1 ≤ u` and `hodd` fix the precision and odd units. The initial integer `e₀` is arbitrary. The existential functions `e` and `z` satisfy the displayed recurrence and $|e_{i+1}|\le2^{v_i+u-1}$ for $i<m$. The free corrections $z_i$ are not constrained to come from divisor counts.

ties.name: Erdos249257.SeamTwoSidedDyadicCellEscape.twoSided
ties.plain: Cell conditions propagate the two-sided bound

rows.name: Erdos249257.SeamTwoSidedDyadicCellEscape.twoSided
rows.plain: Cell conditions propagate the two-sided bound
rows.annotation: Assuming the two-sided cell condition, every row $s\ge5$ has either remainder at most $2^s$ or overshoot at most $2^s$. Lean takes `hescape : SeamTwoSidedDyadicCellEscape`, together with `hs : 5 ≤ s`. At least one of the two bounds holds at each row. The finite base case starts the induction, while `hescape` supplies the branch inequalities needed to continue it at all later rows.

rows.name: Erdos249257.SeamTwoSidedDyadicCellEscape
rows.annotation: The two-sided cell condition prescribes two implications at every row $s\ge5$ without an upper carry. On a middle branch it excludes the signed coordinates $-3,-2,-1$. On a right branch whose overshoot is at most $2^s$, it bounds the upper pulse by $2^{s+2}$. The branch comparisons and the no-carry antecedent are part of the definition. The exclusions are not demands on every row regardless of branch, and the declaration proves none of these conditions.

ties.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_upper_branch_needs_no_exceptional_cell
ties.plain: An upper reset stays below target

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_upper_branch_needs_no_exceptional_cell
rows.plain: An upper reset stays below target
rows.annotation: An upper transition at row $s\ge5$ leaves $\mathrm{rem}(s+1)\le2^{s+1}$. The assumptions are `hs` and the carry condition `hcarry`. The theorem also states that the reset charge is nonnegative and that adding it to the successor remainder gives exactly $2^{s+1}$. This proves the upper branch’s contribution to the two-sided induction without a middle-cell exclusion.

ties.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_upper_branch_needs_no_exceptional_cell
ties.plain: An upper reset stays below target

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_upper_branch_needs_no_exceptional_cell
rows.plain: An upper reset stays below target
rows.annotation: An upper transition at row $s\ge5$ leaves $\mathrm{rem}(s+1)\le2^{s+1}$. The assumptions are `hs` and the carry condition `hcarry`. The theorem also states that the reset charge is nonnegative and that adding it to the successor remainder gives exactly $2^{s+1}$. This proves the upper branch’s contribution to the two-sided induction without a middle-cell exclusion.

ties.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_final_middle_cell_at_least_neg_two
ties.plain: A final middle coordinate exceeds minus-three

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_final_middle_cell_at_least_neg_two
rows.plain: A final middle coordinate exceeds minus-three
rows.annotation: At a middle transition $D\ge13$ followed by right transitions forever, the pulse satisfies $p_D^-+2\le4\mathrm{rem}(D)$. Hence $C_D=4\mathrm{rem}(D)-p_D^- -4\ge-2$. The binders `hncarry` and `hmiddle` identify the middle branch. `hright` supplies the all-right tail. The declaration excludes every $C_D\le-3$ only under that tail assumption. It does not prove this exclusion at arbitrary middle rows.

ties.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_final_middle_cell_at_least_neg_two
ties.plain: A final middle coordinate exceeds minus-three

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_final_middle_cell_at_least_neg_two
rows.plain: A final middle coordinate exceeds minus-three
rows.annotation: At a middle transition $D\ge13$ followed by right transitions forever, the pulse satisfies $p_D^-+2\le4\mathrm{rem}(D)$. Hence $C_D=4\mathrm{rem}(D)-p_D^- -4\ge-2$. The binders `hncarry` and `hmiddle` identify the middle branch. `hright` supplies the all-right tail. The declaration excludes every $C_D\le-3$ only under that tail assumption. It does not prove this exclusion at arbitrary middle rows.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_final_middle_cell_remaining_cells
rows.annotation: At a final middle row $D\ge13$, if $C_D$ lies in $\{-3,-2,-1\}$, it lies in $\{-2,-1\}$. The assumptions `hncarry`, `hmiddle` and `hright` describe that final middle configuration. The final implication in the statement retains membership in the three-element exceptional set as a premise. Therefore the theorem permits nonnegative coordinates and does not assert that every final middle coordinate is $-2$ or $-1$.

ties.name: Erdos249257.middleProducer_allRight_forces_carry_lt_tail
ties.plain: Final middle carry lies below tail

rows.name: Erdos249257.middleProducer_allRight_forces_carry_lt_tail
rows.plain: Final middle carry lies below tail
rows.annotation: At a middle row $D\ge13$ followed by an all-right tail, the producer carry is smaller than the coefficient tail of its augmented finite support at $2D+2$. The assumptions `hncarry`, `hmiddle` and `hright` identify that configuration. The tail uses the below support with $D$ inserted. An independently proved inequality in the opposite direction would contradict this configuration.

rows.name: Erdos249257.SeamMiddleProducerTailEscapeExceptNegThree
rows.annotation: At every no-carry middle transition $s\ge13$ whose middle coordinate is not $-3$, this condition asks that the binary coefficient tail at $2s+2$ of the finite producer support be strictly smaller than its producer carry. The support is the below word with rank $s$ inserted. The exclusion of $-3$ is deliberate because that final-middle case is already impossible. The condition still covers all other indicated middle rows.

ties.name: Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_middleProducerTailEscapeExceptNegThree
ties.plain: A reduced tail condition gives membership

rows.name: Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_middleProducerTailEscapeExceptNegThree
rows.plain: A reduced tail condition gives membership
rows.annotation: If every late middle row other than coordinate $-3$ has producer carry above its coefficient tail, then $1/2\in\mathcal A$. The argument `hmiddleEscape` supplies this unbounded condition. The exceptional value is handled by a separate impossibility theorem for a final middle transition. The premise applies to all the remaining middle coordinates, not just the values $-2$ and $-1$.

ties.name: Erdos249257.SeamMiddleProducerCardEscape
ties.plain: A cardinality bound for middle producers

rows.name: Erdos249257.SeamMiddleProducerCardEscape
rows.plain: A cardinality bound for middle producers
rows.annotation: The condition that at each middle row $s\ge13$, the number of ranks in the below support plus the lower pulse and $5$ is strictly less than $4\mathrm{rem}(s)$. The definition explicitly includes failure of the upper carry and the middle-branch inequality. This sufficient bound controls the complete incidence tail using the finite support size. It is not asserted to be necessary.

ties.name: Erdos249257.SeamMiddleProducerRowEscape
ties.plain: Row bounds at every middle transition

rows.name: Erdos249257.SeamMiddleProducerRowEscape
rows.plain: Row bounds at every middle transition
rows.annotation: The condition that the source remainder is at least its row index at every middle transition $s\ge13$. Lean lists the absence of an upper carry and the strict middle inequality before the conclusion $s\le\mathrm{rem}(s)$. It is a statement about the source row, not its successor. The declaration defines this unbounded hypothesis. It does not prove it from the branch conditions.

rows.fidelity_note: The identity assumes only $r \le \rho$; it holds for every natural $m$, whereas the paper restricts the family to $m \ge 2$.
rows.name: Erdos249257.balancedPulse_weighted_pair
rows.annotation: The identity assumes only $r \le \rho$. It holds for every natural $m$, whereas the paper restricts the family to $m \ge 2$.

ties.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_pulse_family_no_autonomous_decoder
ties.plain: A constant state cannot decode pulses

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_pulse_family_no_autonomous_decoder
rows.plain: A constant state cannot decode pulses
rows.annotation: If every parameter of the balanced-pulse family has the same state, no decoder can recover all parameters from those states. The assumptions are `hm : 2 ≤ m` and `hstate`. There are at least two parameters at this range of $m$, so identical input states cannot decode to distinct values. The theorem concerns this abstract family and constant-state encoding. It does not say the actual Mersenne orbit realises the family.

rows.fidelity_note: The count holds for every $m \ge 0$; the paper introduces this family at $m \ge 2$.
rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_balanced_pulse_fanout_is_radius_succ
rows.annotation: The balanced-pulse family at location $m$ contains exactly $\rho+1=\lfloor(m+1)/2\rfloor+1$ distinct coefficient sequences. The count holds for every $m \ge 0$. The paper introduces this family at $m \ge 2$.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_balanced_pulse_fanout_unbounded_corrected
rows.annotation: The number of balanced-pulse coefficient sequences at location $m$ is at least $\lfloor m/2\rfloor+1$, and these cardinalities are unbounded. The second conjunct explicitly says that every natural bound $N$ is attained or exceeded at some location. No assertion concerns a single Mersenne or totient orbit. This supplies the growing family used in the abstract finite-state restriction.

rows.fidelity_note: The finite-state cardinality bound holds for every natural $m$, without the printed restriction $m \ge 2$.
rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_pulse_family_finite_state_card
rows.annotation: The finite-state cardinality bound holds for every natural $m$, without the printed restriction $m \ge 2$.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_mobius_support_overshoots_half
rows.annotation: The first conjunct is an exact evaluation over positive indices, with `moebius` cast to a real before division. It identifies the signed sum with $1/2$.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_mobius_support_overshoots_half
rows.annotation: The second conjunct rearranges the signed identity into a sum over negative Möbius indices. `positiveMobiusTailTerm` excludes the contribution at $d=1$, so the excess over half is the remaining positive Möbius sum.

rows.annotation: The finite phase $\Theta_L(M)$ equals the sum over divisors $d\ge2$ of the weights $2^{-i}$ at offsets with $d\mid M+i$. The assumptions `hM` and `_hL` require $M,L\ge1$. rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.ShortWindowDivisorPhase.iLeast
rows.annotation: The offset is $i_d(M)=d-(M\bmod d)$. For positive $d$, it lies in $[1,d]$ and is the first positive offset at which $d$ divides $M+i$. In particular, an already divisible starting index gives offset $d$ because the window begins at $i=1$. The definition itself accepts all natural arguments. The accompanying least-offset theorem supplies the positive-divisor interpretation.

rows.fidelity_note: The range theorem allows every $d \ge 1$ and $M \ge 0$; the paper’s divisor sum uses $d \ge 2$ and $M \ge 1$.

Together with its range and the exclusion of smaller positive offsets, it identifies where each geometric progression begins. The divisibility theorem allows every $d \ge 1$ and $M \ge 0$.

This establishes the minimality part of the paper’s description. It does not exclude offset zero when $d\mid M$, because the relevant progression begins strictly after $M$. The minimality theorem allows every $d \ge 1$ and $M \ge 0$.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.ShortWindowDivisorPhase.mCount
rows.plain: Count divisible offsets in the window
rows.annotation: This natural number counts offsets $i$ in the closed interval $[1,L]$ for which $d\mid M+i$. It is the number of terms in the geometric progression beginning at $i_d(M)$ and advancing by $d$. A zero count means that divisor contributes nothing to the window. The count depends on the starting index, divisor and window length, so it must not be treated as a fixed multiplicity.

rows.annotation: If the window ends before the first positive divisible offset, it contains no multiple of the divisor. The assumptions are `hd : 1 ≤ d` and `h : L < iLeast d M`. The conclusion sets the offset count `mCount d M L` to zero. This justifies treating the corresponding residue progression as empty rather than beginning it outside the window.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.ShortWindowDivisorPhase.geometric_term_eq_zero_of_lt_iLeast
rows.annotation: When $L<i_d(M)$ and $d\ge1$, the geometric contribution of divisor $d$ is zero. The binders `h` and `hd` retain those restrictions. The offset count is zero, so the numerator $1-2^{-dm_d}$ vanishes. This is the formula-level counterpart of an empty filtered sum in the divisor-residue expansion.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.ShortWindowDivisorPhase.theta_eq_divisorResidueSum
rows.annotation: If $D\ge M+L$, the phase equals the finite residue sum over $2\le d\le D$. The binders `hM`, `_hL` and `hD` give $M,L\ge1$ and the cutoff bound. No larger divisor divides one of the positive integers $M+1,\ldots,M+L$. A cutoff chosen for one starting index cannot automatically be reused at a larger starting index.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.ShortWindowDivisorPhase.Psi_eq_of_residues_eq
rows.annotation: With $L$ and $D$ fixed, starting indices having the same residues modulo every $2\le d\le D$ give equal values of $\Psi_{L,D}$. The binder `h` lists exactly these residue equalities. The theorem imposes no positivity requirement on the two starting indices. It concerns the fixed-cutoff function, not $\Theta_L$ with a cutoff that changes from one starting index to another.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.ShortWindowDivisorPhase.theta_one_one
rows.annotation: The one-term phase after $M=1$ is $\Theta_1(1)=1/2$, because $2$ has exactly one divisor other than $1$. This exact rational evaluation has no hypotheses. It is paired with the evaluation after $M=3$ to show why residues below a cutoff valid for the first input do not determine the full phase at the second.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.ShortWindowDivisorPhase.theta_one_three
rows.annotation: `theta_one_three` evaluates the second phase in the counterexample. At $M=3$ the coefficient of the sole term is the count of divisors $2$ and $4$ of $M+1$, so $\Theta_1(3)=2/2=1$. The phase at $M=1$ is a separate evaluation.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.ShortWindowDivisorPhase.residue_cutoff_reading_fails
rows.plain: A moving cutoff breaks the inference
rows.annotation: The starting indices $1$ and $3$ agree modulo every divisor in the cutoff interval $[2,2]$, but their one-term phases differ. The statement is an explicit conjunction of residue agreement and phase inequality. The cutoff $2$ covers the first input’s window but misses divisor $4$ at the second. Thus the fixed-cutoff residue theorem cannot be applied to an unrestricted change of starting index.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.ShortWindowDivisorPhase.card_divisors_sub_one
rows.annotation: For a positive integer $n$, its divisor count minus one equals the number of divisors at least $2$. The binder `hn : 1 ≤ n` is required. The subtraction removes the divisor $1$, which is present for every positive $n$. This is the counting identity that turns $\tau(M+i)-1$ into a sum of divisibility indicators.

rows.annotation: Half-membership is equivalent to the actual greedy support’s integer carry returning cofinally often to the prescribed upper strip. `GreedyHalfCarryCofinalStripReturn` quantifies over every lower bound and finds a later index with carry at most `halfStripBound` at its successor. rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_terminal_strip_equiv
rows.plain: Terminal carry bounds and half membership
rows.annotation: One half is represented exactly when arbitrarily large depths $M$ admit a finite support $D\subseteq\{2,\ldots,M\}$ with $|\operatorname{ihc}(D,M-1)|\le2\lfloor\sqrt M\rfloor+4$. Lean also identifies this expanded condition with `HalfCarryCofinalTerminalOnlyStrip`. Supports at different depths need not agree. `Nat.sqrt M` is the integer square root, and the absolute value is taken after casting the carry to a real number. This is an equivalence, not a theorem producing the finite supports.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paper_square_depth_terminal_bound
rows.annotation: At a square depth $M=k^2$, an achieving support has terminal carry at most $2k+4$. Lean assumes `hone : 1 ∉ A`, `hhalf : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = 1 / 2`, and `hk : 1 ≤ k`. Its three conjuncts identify the carry with a coefficient tail, bound that tail, and identify the integer strip bound with $2k+4$. The restriction to square depths makes the constant four sufficient without a rounding loss.

rows.annotation: For a support omitting rank $1$, the integer half-carry at $N$ equals $2^{N+1}(1/2-X_A(2))$ plus its divisor-coefficient tail at $N+1$. The hypothesis is `hone`. The scale $2^{N+1}$ makes any nonzero value error dominate a square-root carry envelope. The tail term remains present until the support value is known. It cannot simply be discarded.

rows.name: Erdos249257.erdosSupportSeries
rows.annotation: The sum $X_A(b)=\sum_{a\in A}(b^a-1)^{-1}$, with the paper mainly using $b=2$. The definition takes a natural-number base `b` and a set `A : Set ℕ`, and an indicator makes terms outside $A$ zero. It imposes no infinitude or irrationality hypothesis. Results about convergence and irrationality state their own assumptions, usually `hb : 2 ≤ b`. The paper uses positive exponents. Lean also permits zero, whose term is zero under its division convention.

rows.name: Erdos249257.supportCoeff
rows.annotation: The coefficient $c_A(n)$ counts the positive divisors of $n$ that lie in $A$. For example, when $n=6$, it counts whichever of $1,2,3,6$ belong to the support. In Lean, `n.divisors.filter` keeps precisely those divisors and `.card` counts them. This is a definition for any set `A`, with no sparsity, infinitude or rationality assumption. These integer coefficients connect the reciprocal Mersenne sum with its binary generating series.

rows.name: Erdos249257.mersenneAchievementSet
rows.annotation: The set $\mathcal A$ of values represented by choosing any collection of positive reciprocal Mersenne terms. Membership means that a support `A : Set ℕ` exists with `0 ∉ A` and the specified sum equal to the target. This definition allows finite and infinite supports. It does not assert that a particular rational number belongs to the set. The half-membership and one-twenty-first questions are separate existence claims.

For $x=1/2$, the paper denotes this support by $G$.

rows.name: Erdos249257.ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow
rows.annotation: An exact row at depth $n$ is a finite set $D\subseteq\{2,\ldots,n\}$ whose integer quotient sum is $2^{n-1}-1$. Lean writes this as an existential proposition `ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow n`. Both subtraction and the exponent $n-1$ use natural-number conventions. The paper uses positive depths. The definition only describes a candidate row. A theorem or hypothesis must provide the set $D$, and rows at different depths are not required to share a support.

rows.name: Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_cofinalExactLocalRows
rows.annotation: If exact finite quotient rows occur at unbounded depths, one half belongs to the achievement set. The assumption `hcofinal : CofinalExactLocalMersenneHalfRows` supplies those rows. Their values approach one half, and closedness of the achievement set gives a representing support. The theorem needs no compatibility between the row witnesses and states no algorithm for recovering the limiting support. Its conclusion is membership, which itself means that some representing support exists.

rows.name: Erdos249257.continuous_positiveMersenneDigitValue
rows.annotation: The map sending a sequence of zero-one choices to its reciprocal Mersenne sum is continuous. No assumption about a target or its representation is required. Agreement on a sufficiently long initial segment makes the remaining contribution small, because the common tail bound tends to zero. In Lean this is `Continuous positiveMersenneDigitValue`. Together with compactness of the digit space, continuity supports the passage from arbitrarily accurate finite approximations to a represented limiting value.

rows.name: Erdos249257.two_mem_of_exact_localMersenneQuotient

Lean assumes `hn : 3 ≤ n`, the range condition `hD`, and the target equality `hquot : localPrefixQuotient D n = 2 ^ (n - 1) - 1`. The result applies to each row separately. It explains why a limiting support extracted from arbitrarily deep rows can retain exponent two, but this declaration itself does not construct that limiting support.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR20.half_mem_iff_cofinal_exact_rows
rows.annotation: Representation of one half is equivalent to exact finite quotient rows at unbounded depths. This declaration supplies both directions, as the paper's Section 12.8 table states. The equivalence does not construct rows without an assumption or settle half-membership. Here $D$ is a finite set of exponents and $Q(D,M)$ is its local quotient sum at depth $M$. Lean returns a natural number, so subtraction truncates at zero. Later algebraic uses must supply inequalities that prevent truncation. This definition alone does not say that the prefix lies below a target or that the remainder can be filled.

ties.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.frameLcm
ties.plain: Common period of the finite support

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.frameLcm
rows.plain: Common period of the finite support
rows.annotation: The least common multiple $Q=\operatorname{lcm}(F)$ of the finitely many exponents in $F$. Lean uses `F.lcm id`, with the empty-set convention $Q=1$. For a support of positive exponents, each residue-dependent kernel repeats after $Q$, so the potential has this period. This definition supplies a permissible common period. It does not claim that $Q$ is the smallest period of every function subsequently built from that potential.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.incidenceCount
rows.annotation: The finite-support divisor count $f_F(n)=\#\{a\in F:a\mid n\}$. Lean filters the finite set `F` by divisibility and takes its cardinality. Only divisors of $n$ that already lie in $F$ contribute. The definition is valid for any finite set. In this section the paper assumes positive exponents so that the reciprocal Mersenne kernels and their common period have the intended meaning.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.framePotential
rows.plain: Shifted potential of a finite support
rows.annotation: The potential $U_F(N)$ is the sum of the base-two geometric kernels associated with the finite support $F$. Lean writes `∑ a ∈ F, kernelWeight 2 a N`, which equals $\sum_{a\in F}2^{N\bmod a}/(2^a-1)$ for positive exponents. The variable $N$ is the observation shift, not an exponent selected into the support. A separate identity expresses the same potential as the weighted sum of future divisor counts.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.framePotential_eq_tsum
rows.annotation: For a finite support of positive exponents, $U_F(N)=\sum_{r\ge1}2^{-r}f_F(N+r)$. Lean assumes `hF : 0 ∉ F` and indexes the sum from zero using `r + 1`, so its weight is $(1/2)^{r+1}$. This identity connects the periodic residue formula for the potential with the probabilistic proof, where a large divisor count at one future offset can force the entire potential above one.

rows.fidelity_note: The source defines sInf (logMajorantCosts F t), an infimum. The displayed minimum additionally claims attainment; no attainment theorem was found in the relevant source module.
rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.kappaOne
rows.annotation: `kappaOne` is `sInf (logMajorantCosts F t)`, the infimum of the costs of admissible logarithmic majorants. Writing a minimum in (17) additionally requires a coefficient family attaining that infimum.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.logMajorantCosts
rows.note: The admissibility constraints and coefficient cost inside the optimisation.
rows.annotation: The admissibility constraints and coefficient cost inside the optimisation. A candidate coefficient sequence `c` must dominate the logarithm at every divisor of $Q=\operatorname{lcm}(F)$, and its cost is $\sum_{d\mid Q}c_d/d$.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.log_incidence_le_divisorMajorant
rows.plain: Divisor constraints control every positive integer
rows.annotation: A logarithmic majorant imposed on divisors of $Q$ controls the same logarithm at every positive integer $n$. The inputs are `hF : 0 ∉ F`, the divisor constraints `hcon`, and `hn : 0 < n`. The reason is that a member of $F$ divides $n$ exactly when it divides $\gcd(n,Q)$. Thus the finite constraint set used in defining the cost is sufficient for the later estimates over all observation offsets.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.logMajorantCosts_nonempty
rows.annotation: For every finite set $F$ and positive threshold $t$, there is an admissible logarithmic divisor majorant. The only numerical assumption is `ht : 0 < t`. This theorem does not require $F$ to be nonempty. Its conclusion is nonemptiness of the set of costs, not attainment of the infimum. It supplies the feasibility needed before reasoning about $\kappa_1(F;t)$ as an optimisation over admissible majorants.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.paperCoverCost
rows.annotation: The infimum $K_*(F)$ over the paper's finite and countable fractional covers. The source defines `paperCoverCost A` as the infimum of the union of the admissible countable-cover costs and finite-cover costs. These covers allow overlapping finite sets, positive weights summing to one, and exponents in $(0,1]$. This optimises fractional power majorants, whereas $\kappa_1$ optimises one logarithmic divisor majorant. The two costs are separate mathematical quantities.

This count controls the exponential number of encoded exponents dividing $n$, once the parent prime also divides $n$.

rows.note: For the divisor moduli used in the displayed maximum; the formal proof uses an epsilon contradiction.
rows.plain: Every cover pays the arithmetic probability
rows.annotation: For a positive finite support and positive divisor $\ell$ of its common period, the arithmetic exceedance probability is no larger than the cost of any admissible fractional cover. Lean assumes `hF`, `hℓ0`, `hℓ`, and supplies the cover as `C`. The proof sends the observation scale and then the averaging width to infinity. Only the original finite support needs a common period. rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.logarithmic_initial_interval
rows.annotation: For positive finite nonempty $F$, the fraction of integers $1\le N\le X$ with $U_F(N)>t$ is at most $2\kappa_1(F;t)/\log(4/3)$. The statement has no arbitrary arithmetic-progression modulus and therefore does not contradict the preceding counterexample.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.divisorMajorant_le_cost_mul
rows.annotation: A nonnegative divisor majorant $g(n)$ is at most its reciprocal cost times $n$. Lean assumes `hc` for coefficient nonnegativity, `hD` for positive divisor moduli, and `hn : 0 < n`. Each contributing modulus divides $n$, so it is at most $n$, giving $c_d\le n(c_d/d)$. This elementary bound limits how far a witnessing offset can lie beyond an observation point in the initial-interval argument.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR21.exists_offset_of_framePotential_gt

rows.annotation: If $U_F(N)>t>0$, some positive offset $r$ has $\log(1+f_F(N+r)/t)>r\log(4/3)$. The hypotheses are `hF`, `ht`, and `hgt`. If every offset failed this strict comparison, the divisor counts would be bounded by $t((4/3)^r-1)$, whose weighted geometric sum is $t$. This contradicts exceedance and provides the offset counted in the union-bound proof.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.coverGauge
rows.annotation: The least scalar cost obtainable by choosing an exponent $0<\alpha\le1$. For a nonzero real parameter $t$, `coverGauge t` is the infimum of the values $t^\alpha/(2^\alpha-1)$ in `scalarCoverCosts t`. The value at zero is defined separately to be zero. The infimum need not come with a minimizer merely by definition. The small- and large-parameter theorems identify the value and, in their ranges, exhibit an admissible exponent attaining it.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.coverLogParameter
rows.annotation: The base-two logarithm $z=\log_2t$, written in Lean as `Real.log t / Real.log 2`. This definition accepts any real `t`, but the scalar minimization argument uses positive parameters, and its large branch assumes $t>4$. Substituting $y=2^\alpha$ changes the original scalar cost to $y^z/(y-1)$. The parameter records that change of variables without changing the base or introducing an extra logarithmic factor.

rows.annotation: The branch above four, with $z$ equal to the base-two logarithm. For $t>4$, the optimal scalar cost is $z^z/(z-1)^{z-1}$, where $z=\log_2t$.

rows.name: Erdos249257.erdos257_family_factorial_instance
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: The reciprocal Mersenne sum over exponents $(k+1)!$ is irrational. This source statement is an unconditional instance with no supplied support hypotheses. Its exponents are factorials, and they are not a pairwise-coprime sequence. The instance belongs with the least-common-multiple gap method, as the earlier support table records. The supplementary list's heading “Pairwise-coprime supports” should therefore not be read as the hypothesis behind this particular theorem.

rows.name: Erdos249257.erdos257_family_two_pow_instance
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: The sum $\sum_{k\ge0}(2^{2^k}-1)^{-1}$ is irrational. The exponent set is $1,2,4,8,\ldots$, and the source supplies this as an unconditional theorem. These exponents are not pairwise coprime, so the neighbouring pairwise-coprime theorem is not the route by which this example is justified. It is an instance of the least-common-multiple gap argument described earlier in the paper.

rows.name: Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_pairwise_coprime
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: An infinite pairwise-coprime support with summable reciprocals has irrational support series at every integer base $b\ge2$. The hypotheses are `hb`, `hA`, `hpair` and `hsum`. Reciprocal summability is a separate assumption from coprimality. In particular, this declaration cannot be applied to all primes merely because distinct primes are coprime. The reciprocal-sum condition must also hold.

rows.name: Erdos249257.irrational_ratWeightSeries_eventuallyPeriodic
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: An eventually periodic nonnegative rational weighting of the reciprocal Mersenne terms has irrational sum when its periodic tail has a positive weight. Lean assumes `hb : 2 ≤ b`, `hm : 0 < m`, nonnegativity `hγ0`, periodicity after $N_0$ through `hper`, and `hpos` at a positive index at or beyond $N_0$. The statement does not cover arbitrary signed eventually periodic weights. The finite initial part is allowed to differ from the periodic tail.

rows.name: Erdos249257.SupportSunflowerDichotomy.sunflowerForcedCarrySupply_of_orthogonalPetalBouquet
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: For the stated fixed-core support structure, the forced-slot tail-selection hypothesis yields the full family of carry certificates. The source requires both `hB : OrthogonalPetalBouquet A` and `hselection : SunflowerForcedSlotTailSelection A`. The first describes finite core factors and coprime petals with summable reciprocal mass. The second supplies suitable openings with bounded tails. The support structure alone is not the entire antecedent of this declaration.

rows.name: Erdos249257.SupportSunflowerDichotomy.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_of_orthogonalPetalBouquet
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: At base $2$, an orthogonal-petal bouquet support has irrational value if it also satisfies the forced-slot tail-selection condition. The declaration takes two independent assumptions, `hB` and `hselection`. The structural hypothesis controls cores and coprime petals. The selection hypothesis supplies suitable late tails at every required precision. This theorem does not claim that the bouquet structure by itself proves the tail-selection condition.

rows.name: Erdos249257.finite_period_noncollapse_rat_den
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: For a nonempty finite support of positive exponents and integer base $b\ge2$, the multiplicative order of $b$ modulo the reduced denominator of the finite sum equals the least common multiple of the exponents. Lean assumes `hF`, `h0`, and `hb`. `orderOf` measures the period of powers in the corresponding unit group. The theorem says that cancellation in the rational sum does not shorten this arithmetic period. It does not assert that the denominator is the unreduced product.

ties.name: Erdos249257.exists_normalized_support_fraction_iff_exists_booleanMobiusCarry
ties.plain: Rational support values and Boolean carries

rows.name: Erdos249257.exists_normalized_support_fraction_iff_exists_booleanMobiusCarry
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: Rational support values and Boolean carries
rows.annotation: A positive nonempty normalised support represents $p/q$ exactly when an integer sequence satisfies the Boolean Möbius carry certificate. Lean assumes only `hq : 0 < q` before stating the equivalence. The certificate requires initial value $p$, positive carries, a square-root bound, divisible recurrence differences, and zero-one Möbius inversion. Its existence is equivalent to existence of a support, not automatically supplied by the equivalence. The support need not be infinite in this statement.

rows.name: Erdos249257.binaryCoeffSeries_rational_iff_exists_temperedBinaryOrbit
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: For coefficients $0\le c(n)\le n$, the binary coefficient series is rational exactly when some positive integer $v$ admits an integer recurrence $u_{N+1}=2u_N-vc(N+1)$ with $u_N/2^N\to0$. The growth hypothesis is `hgrowth`. Lean packages the recurrence and limiting condition as `IsTemperedBinaryOrbit`. The decay requirement is essential to identify the recurrence with the series value, and merely solving the recurrence in integers does not give this rationality criterion.

ties.name: Erdos249257.one_div_oddOrder_le_reciprocalMass_of_support_fraction
ties.plain: Reciprocal mass bounds the odd-denominator order

rows.name: Erdos249257.one_div_oddOrder_le_reciprocalMass_of_support_fraction
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: Reciprocal mass bounds the odd-denominator order
rows.annotation: A support representing $p/(2^cv)$ has reciprocal mass at least $1/\operatorname{ord}_v(2)$ under the stated normalisation and summability assumptions. Lean requires a positive support element `hA`, reciprocal summability `hsum`, `hv : 1 < v`, oddness `hvodd`, coprimality `hpv`, and the value identity `hvalue`. The order is that of doubling modulo the odd denominator. This is a restriction on a hypothetical rational representation, not a construction of one.

ties.name: Erdos249257.exists_unbounded_shifted_odd_tail_nat_state_of_support_fraction
ties.plain: Rational infinite supports force unbounded carries

rows.name: Erdos249257.exists_unbounded_shifted_odd_tail_nat_state_of_support_fraction
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: Rational infinite supports force unbounded carries
rows.annotation: An infinite support with rational value $p/(2^cv)$ and $v>0$ gives positive natural-number tail states after the shift $c$. Lean assumes `hAinf`, `hv`, and `hvalue`, and produces a sequence obeying the exact doubling recurrence, the congruence modulo $v$, and unboundedness. Although the name refers to an odd tail, this declaration itself assumes only positivity of $v$. The last quantifier is $\forall B\,\exists n$, which means unbounded values, not convergence to infinity.

rows.name: Erdos249257.supportCoeffZeroWindow_length_le_eps_logb_add
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: Under a rational support-value identity, every run of zero divisor counts beyond the fixed shift has length at most $\varepsilon\log_2(N+1)+B$ for any chosen $\varepsilon>0$. Lean assumes a positive support element `hA`, positive denominator factor `hv`, the rational value `hvalue`, and `hε`. The resulting constant $B\ge0$ may depend on these data. This conditional asymptotic estimate is distinct from the elementary bound supplied by any fixed supported divisor.

ties.name: Erdos249257.volume_mersenneAchievementSet
ties.plain: The achievement set has measure one

rows.name: Erdos249257.volume_mersenneAchievementSet
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: The achievement set has measure one
rows.annotation: The full reciprocal Mersenne achievement set has Lebesgue measure one. Lean states `volume mersenneAchievementSet = 1` without any target-specific hypothesis. Measure records the total size of the set on the real line. It does not decide whether a particular point, such as one half or one twenty-first, belongs to the set. The set can have positive measure while also being nowhere dense.

rows.name: Erdos249257.perfect_mersenneAchievementSet
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: The reciprocal Mersenne achievement set is perfect because it is closed and has no isolated points. The theorem is unconditional. Changing a sufficiently late digit gives a distinct represented value arbitrarily close to the original value, while compactness supplies closedness. This geometric property does not force membership of a prescribed rational point. It describes how represented points accumulate on one another, rather than which rational numbers occur.

rows.name: Erdos249257.isTotallyDisconnected_mersenneAchievementSet
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: The achievement set is totally disconnected, so every connected subset contains at most one point. Lean states this property for the entire Mersenne achievement set without further assumptions. Strict separation between finite digit choices prevents an interval of represented values. Total disconnectedness is compatible with the set's positive Lebesgue measure and does not determine whether any specified rational target is represented.

ties.name: Erdos249257.isNowhereDense_mersenneAchievementSet
ties.plain: The achievement set is nowhere dense

rows.name: Erdos249257.isNowhereDense_mersenneAchievementSet
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: The achievement set is nowhere dense
rows.annotation: The achievement set is nowhere dense, so its closure contains no nonempty open interval. Since it is already closed, every open interval contains a smaller open interval disjoint from it. The source theorem has no additional hypotheses. This topological conclusion does not imply measure zero and does not exclude a chosen rational target. The independent measure theorem gives the set measure one.

ties.name: Erdos249257.mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_greedy_survival
ties.plain: Membership is survival at every rank

rows.name: Erdos249257.mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_greedy_survival
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: Membership is survival at every rank
rows.annotation: A real target $x$ lies in the Mersenne achievement set exactly when it is nonnegative and its greedy remainder never exceeds the complete tail. The declaration is an equivalence for every real `x`. The quantifier over ranks is universal and unbounded. A single larger remainder therefore excludes membership, while a finite list of successful comparisons supplies only the listed ranks.

rows.name: Erdos249257.three_fourths_not_mem_mersenneAchievementSet
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: The target $3/4$ is not a reciprocal Mersenne subseries value. This is an unconditional point-specific exclusion, unlike the general topological properties of the achievement set. The greedy test encounters a remainder larger than the entire remaining tail, so no later choices can fill the gap. The theorem concerns this target alone and yields no exclusion of one half or one twenty-first.

ties.name: Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_greedySkippedSupport_infinite
ties.plain: Half membership and infinitely many skips

rows.name: Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_greedySkippedSupport_infinite
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: Half membership and infinitely many skips
rows.annotation: The greedy form uses omitted positive exponents at target $1/2$. `Infinite` of that set is equivalent to representation, so either a proof of infinitely many skips or a proof of membership would settle both conditions.

rows.name: Erdos249257.HalfCarryReachability.finite_boolSupport_ne_half
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: A finite support of positive exponents cannot have value $1/2$. Lean assumes `hfinite : A.Finite` and `hzero : 0 ∉ A`. It does not assume anything about a greedy construction. Every denominator $2^a-1$ is odd, so a finite sum has odd reduced denominator and cannot equal one half. Consequently any support representing $1/2$ must be infinite. That consequence still requires a representing support to exist.

rows.name: ErdosProblems.Erdos257.volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_dichotomy
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: Restrict the available digit positions to a set $J$. If only a finite set $F$ of positions is forbidden, the restricted achievement set has measure $2^{-|F|}$, and if infinitely many positions are forbidden, it has measure zero. The theorem states this dichotomy for every `J : Set ℕ`. These are zero-based digit positions, with position $k$ controlling exponent $k+1$. The conclusion concerns measure, not rational membership.

rows.name: Erdos249257.CofinalPositiveHalfGreedySkips
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: The condition that for every lower bound $N$ there is a skipped rank $c\ge\max(N,4)$ with positive half-greedy remainder before that rank. In Lean the skip is the strict comparison `greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 2) (c - 1) < mersenneWeightRat c`. The condition is a proposition, not an existence theorem. Requiring $c\ge4$ discards only initial ranks and does not change what it means for skipped ranks to be unbounded.

ties.name: Erdos249257.exactLocalMersenneHalfRow_of_positiveHalfGreedySkip
ties.plain: One skip gives an exact row

rows.name: Erdos249257.exactLocalMersenneHalfRow_of_positiveHalfGreedySkip
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: One skip gives an exact row
rows.annotation: A positive greedy skip at exponent $c\ge4$ gives an exact quotient row at depth $2c-2$. The assumptions `hc`, `hpos` and `hskip` say that the rational greedy remainder immediately before $c$ lies strictly between zero and $1/(2^c-1)$. The conclusion is existence of a finite row, with no separate sharp-capacity hypothesis. It concerns a supplied skip, not the existence of arbitrarily late skips.

rows.name: Erdos249257.cofinalExactLocalMersenneHalfRows_of_positiveHalfGreedySkips
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: Arbitrarily late positive skips of the half-greedy rule yield exact quotient rows at unbounded depths. The only input is `hskips : CofinalPositiveHalfGreedySkips`. A skip at rank $c\ge4$ provides an exact row at depth $2c-2$, so unbounded skipped ranks give unbounded row depths. The theorem proves this implication. It does not establish the required skips. The separate half-membership equivalences explain why the antecedent remains an unresolved existence condition.

rows.name: Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_positiveHalfGreedySkips
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: If the rational half-greedy rule has positive skips at unbounded ranks, then $1/2\in\mathcal A$. The whole premise is `hskips : CofinalPositiveHalfGreedySkips`. Those skips produce exact quotient rows at unbounded endpoints, whose values approach the target. A long finite list of skips is not the premise, and the implication does not itself prove the existence of infinitely many skips.

ties.name: Erdos249257.exists_upperHalfBooleanWord_of_skippedCore
ties.plain: A binary word for loose capacity

rows.name: Erdos249257.exists_upperHalfBooleanWord_of_skippedCore
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: A binary word for loose capacity
rows.annotation: A critical-crossing core at rank $c\ge4$ has a remaining suffix representable by a Boolean word of length $c-1$. Lean assumes `hc`, the support range `hD`, strict below-halfness `hbelow`, and the crossing inequality `hskip`. The conclusion gives a list containing only zero and one whose base-two value is `localBinarySuffix D 1 (2 * c - 2)`. This uses the loose capacity bound. It does not supply the sharper $c-2$-bit fill.

rows.name: Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_unboundedTerminalFalse
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.annotation: One half belongs to the achievement set exactly when seam greedy rows with a false terminal bit occur at arbitrarily large ranks. Lean packages the latter condition as `SeamGreedyUnboundedTerminalFalse`. A false bit means that the corresponding terminal weight is skipped. The theorem establishes an unconditional equivalence between the two propositions. It does not assert the unbounded occurrence of such rows. The finite seam representation is related to the real greedy process by the surrounding source results.

ties.name: Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_exists_unboundedSkippedRanksAlong
ties.plain: Half membership and unbounded skipped ranks

rows.name: Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_exists_unboundedSkippedRanksAlong
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: Half membership and unbounded skipped ranks
rows.annotation: One half is represented exactly when some sequence of seam rows contains skipped ranks tending to infinity. The condition also requires the row depths themselves to tend to infinity. Lean states an existential quantifier over `rows : ℕ → ℕ` and packages the choices and both limits in `SeamGreedyUnboundedSkippedRanksAlong rows`. The skipped coordinate must grow, and repeatedly observing one early skipped bit in later rows would not supply this condition.

ties.name: Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.postTakeUnsafeAt_iff_band
ties.plain: The interval for an unsafe skip

rows.name: Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.postTakeUnsafeAt_iff_band
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: The interval for an unsafe skip
rows.annotation: A last skip after a take is dyadically unsafe precisely when the preceding reciprocal remainder lies in the stated interval. Lean assumes `hR : 0 < R`, `hRq : R < q`, and `hm : 1 ≤ m`. The interval is $(q(m-1)/(q+m-1),qm/(q+m))$. This is a local equivalence for supplied rational parameters. It does not show that the actual half-greedy orbit ever enters, or always avoids, the interval.

ties.name: Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.singletonUnsafe_iff_twoThirdsBand
ties.plain: The band for one intervening skip

rows.name: Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.singletonUnsafe_iff_twoThirdsBand
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: The band for one intervening skip
rows.annotation: For a take followed by exactly one intervening skip, dyadic unsafety is equivalent to the reciprocal remainder lying in the two-thirds band. The hypotheses are `hR : 0 < R` and `hRq : R < q`. This specialises the general interval to the next threshold $m=2q+2$. The statement concerns the singleton-skip configuration, and conclusions derived from this band should not be advertised as applying to arbitrary longer runs of skips.

ties.name: Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.not_twoThirdsBand_of_int
ties.plain: Integral reciprocals avoid the two-thirds band

rows.name: Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.not_twoThirdsBand_of_int
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: Integral reciprocals avoid the two-thirds band
rows.annotation: When both $R$ and the positive $q$ are integers, $R$ cannot lie in the two-thirds band. The assumptions are `hq`, `hRm` and `hqn`. The latter two identify rational parameters with integer casts. The band models the single-skip take–skip–take configuration after a take. This declaration excludes that band only, and interpreting it as a statement about a greedy run requires the corresponding band characterization.

ties.name: Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.seven_le_of_intBand_odd
ties.plain: Odd band data require numerator seven

rows.name: Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.seven_le_of_intBand_odd
rows.note: A supplementary navigation label; the reading note states the full hypotheses.
rows.plain: Odd band data require numerator seven
rows.annotation: Positive odd integers $p,D,q$ in the cleared two-thirds band satisfy $p\ge7$. The binders `hp`, `hD`, `hq`, `hpodd`, `hDodd`, `hqodd` and `hband` give all assumptions. The band defect is divisible by four, forcing the numerator bound. This is the singleton take–skip–take specialization. The theorem does not cover every possible length of unsafe skip run or prove reachability of its data.
